thread.title: Netflix Stock Jumps On Big Increase In New Subscribers

author: Investor's Business Daily
title: Netflix Stock Jumps On Big Increase In New Subscribers
text:
Shutterstock photo
Internet television leader Netflix ( NFLX ) late Monday surprised investors with a huge beat in new subscribers, sending its stock soaring into record high territory in extended trading.
Netflix added 8.33 million new subscribers worldwide in the fourth quarter, vs. its target of 6.3 million.
Netflix stock was up more than 9%, near 248.50, in after-hours trading on the stock market today . During the regular session, it rose 3.2% to 227.58. In intraday trading, Netflix notched an all-time high of 227.79.
Netflix reported earnings per share of 41 cents on sales of $3.29 billion for the December quarter, compared with 15 cents and $2.48 billion in the year-earlier period. Analysts expected Netflix to earn 41 cents a share on sales of $3.26 billion in the fourth quarter, according to Zacks Investment Research.
Netflix added 1.98 million new U.S. streaming subscribers and 6.36 million international subscribers in the fourth quarter. Three months ago, Netflix forecast adding 1.25 million U.S. streaming subscribers and 5.05 million international subscribers.
Netflix ended 2017 with 117.58 million streaming subscribers worldwide, including 54.75 million in the U.S. and 62.83 million in foreign markets.
For the current quarter, Netflix is predicting it will add 6.35 million net new subscribers, including 1.45 million in the U.S. and 4.9 million in other countries.
IBD'S TAKE: Netflix stock has an IBD Composite Rating of 92 out of a best-possible 99. For more analysis on Netflix, visit the IBD Stock Checkup .
For the first quarter, Netflix expects to earn 63 cents a share on sales of $3.69 billion. Analysts were modeling Netflix to earn 57 cents a share, up 43% year over year, on sales of $3.52 billion, up 34%, in the March quarter, Zacks said.
"We had a beautiful Q4, completing a great year as internet TV expands globally," Netflix management said in a letter to shareholders. "In 2017, we grew streaming revenue 36% to over $11 billion, added 24 million new memberships (compared to 19 million in 2016), achieved for the first time a full-year positive international contribution profit, and more than doubled global operating income."
The company credited its strong subscriber gains to its original content efforts and the growth of internet television overall.
"We believe our big investments in content are paying off," Netflix said. "In 2017, average streaming hours per membership grew by 9% year over year. With greater than expected member growth (resulting in more revenue), we now plan to spend $7.5 billion to $8.0 billion on content on a P&L basis in 2018."
Hit original shows in the quarter included "Stranger Things," "13 Reasons Why," "Marvel's The Punisher" and "Mindhunter," the company said. It also called its big-budget fantasy action movie "Bright" a "major success."
On the competitive front, Netflix cited Amazon.com ( AMZN ) and Apple ( AAPL ) as two rivals to watch in the year ahead. It noted Walt Disney ( DIS ) as a streaming competitor in 2019.
"The market for entertainment time is vast and can support many successful services," Netflix said in its shareholder letter. "In addition, entertainment services are often complementary given their unique content offerings. We believe this is largely why both we and Hulu have been able to succeed and grow."
